extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, paralegals, patent attorneys/agents and applicants involved in terminal disclaimers and assignee authorization (MPEP users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, examining, and processing statutory and terminal disclaimers (37 CFR 1.321, 3.73; 35 U.S.C. 253) including required contents, signatures, chain-of-title evidence, form paragraphs, and handling of informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine compliance with 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321 and 3.73 when processing disclaimers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of Corrections Branch (or Examining Group paralegal for pending applications) is responsible for determining compliance, notifying applicant of informal disclaimers, recording disclaimers, and providing disclaimer data for printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature authorization (37 CFR 3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the 'Certificate Under 37 CFR 3.73(b)' may be sent to applicant as an acceptable way to comply. Where the attorney or agent of record signs the disclaimer, there is no need to comply with 37 CFR 3.73(b). The signature on the disclaimer need not be an original signature; copies (photocopy/facsimile) are acceptable per 37 CFR 1.4(d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must be for the terminal portion of entire patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer directed to particular claim(s) will not be accepted; the disclaimer must be of a terminal portion of the term of the entire patent to be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute does not provide for conditional disclaimers; a proposed disclaimer contingent on allowance of certain claims cannot be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of disclaimant, interest, and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclaimer should identify the disclaimant and his/her interest in the application/patent and should specify the date when the disclaimer is to become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required information helps establish who is disclaiming and when the disclaimer applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on continuing applications and CPAs
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer filed to obviate a double patenting rejection is effective only with respect to the application identified in the disclaimer unless by its terms it extends to continuing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A terminal disclaimer filed in a parent application normally has no effect on a continuing application claiming benefits under 35 U.S.C. 120, except it carries over to a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) because the CPA retains the parent's application number. To prevent carryover to a CPA, file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with the required fee requesting the terminal disclaimer not be carried over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimers required in each application for double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more pending applications each justify an obviousness-type double patenting rejection over the other, an appropriate terminal disclaimer must be filed in each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents an improper timewise extension of patent rights in the last application to be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examining Group paralegal processing duties
rubrics_metrics.description: When a terminal disclaimer is filed in an application pending in an Examining Group, the paralegal will determine compliance, notify the examiner whether acceptable, indicate informalities, record the terminal disclaimer, and provide printing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paralegal identifies a terminal disclaimer by attaching a green label to the file wrapper, stamping a notice on the file of the disclaimed term, endorsing the paper on the 'Contents' flap, and entering the terminal disclaimer into PALM system records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to notify applicant of informalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should notify the applicant of any informalities in the terminal disclaimer in the next Office action or by interview if that will expedite prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should initial and date the Terminal Disclaimer Informal Memo and return it to the paralegal to indicate applicant was appropriately notified; the memo may then be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for acceptance and rejection notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 14.23/14.23.01 are used to inform applicant that a terminal disclaimer has been reviewed and accepted; paragraphs 14.24/14.25 to notify that it has NOT been accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow bracket instructions for inserting dates, application/patent numbers, and use specified follow-on paragraphs (14.26–14.32) to indicate reasons for non-acceptance. Use 14.23.01/14.25 for reexamination proceedings when specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of interest must be stated (14.26.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who signed the disclaimer must state the extent of his/her interest or the business entity's interest in the application/patent (37 CFR 1.321(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not stated, use form paragraph 14.26.01 following 14.24/14.25 and 14.26. Provide examiner notes as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer cannot be directed to particular claim(s) (14.26.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer directed to a particular claim or claims is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraphs 14.24/14.25 and 14.26. Refer to MPEP §1490 for discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature required on terminal disclaimer (14.26.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer that is not signed is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.26.03 after 14.24/14.25 and 14.26 to indicate the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/patent must be identified correctly (14.26.04/14.26.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application or patent being disclaimed must be identified; incorrect identification is a defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If improperly identified, indicate correct number. A terminal disclaimer is acceptable if it includes correct Patent Number or correct Application Number (including series code and serial no.), or serial number with proper filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed by all owners when required (14.26.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: If not signed by all owners, supplemental terminal disclaimers are required from the remaining owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.26.06 after 14.24/14.25 and 14.26 to indicate this deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer fee submission requirement and fee handling (14.26.07, 14.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclaimer fee in accordance with 37 CFR 1.20(d) must be submitted unless an authorization to charge a deposit account is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a disclaimer fee was paid for a terminal disclaimer which was not accepted, applicant does not have to pay another disclaimer fee when submitting a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer (use 14.35 to notify applicant/patent owner that fee is not required twice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must include enforceability-during-common-ownership clause (14.27.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclaimer must include a recitation that any patent granted shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patent is commonly owned with the application(s) or patent(s) which formed the basis for the double patenting rejection (37 CFR 1.321(c)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.27.01 following 14.24/14.25 and 14.26 to indicate this omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must disclaim correct terminal period of subject patent/application (14.27.02/14.27.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclaimer must disclaim the terminal portion corresponding to the correct period (e.g., terminal portion of any patent granted on the subject application or of the subject patent in reissue/reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the period disclaimed is incorrect or not specified, use 14.27.02/14.27.03 and provide an example of proper language (see 14.27.04/14.27.05/14.27.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide acceptable example language for disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific example language is provided for situations: provisional obviousness-type double patenting over a pending application; obviousness-type double patenting over a prior patent; reexamination contexts; and language for existing patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the supplied example paragraphs (e.g., 'Petitioner hereby disclaims ... the terminal part of any patent granted on the instant application, which would extend beyond the expiration date of any patent granted on Application No. ...') as models for acceptable disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to state capacity to sign (14.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person signing fails to state capacity to sign for a corporation or business entity and is not established as authorized to act on behalf of the assignee, the disclaimer is deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.28 after 14.24/14.25 and 14.26 to point out this deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signer not recognized as officer of assignee (14.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person who signed the terminal disclaimer is not recognized as a corporate officer and not established as authorized to act for the assignee, use form paragraph 14.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney or agent of record is always authorized to sign the terminal disclaimer even if not an officer. Use 14.29.02 to explain how a non-recognized officer may establish authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepting disclaimer signed by non-recognized officer (14.29.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person other than a recognized officer may execute a terminal disclaimer provided the record includes a statement that the person is empowered to sign terminal disclaimers and/or act on behalf of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new terminal disclaimer including the empowerment statement or a separately filed paper referencing the prior disclaimer with the empowerment suffices. Title is desirable but not mandatory. Send a sample terminal disclaimer with the Office action to show corrective format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of chain of title (37 CFR 3.73; 14.30/14.30.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee must establish ownership interest by submitting documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original inventor(s) to the assignee or by specifying where such evidence is recorded in the Office (e.g., reel and frame number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If absent, the terminal disclaimer is deficient. Note: where an attorney or agent of record signs a terminal disclaimer, there is no need to provide a statement under 37 CFR 3.73(b). Documentary evidence may be in the disclaimer itself or in a separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership submission informal / not signed by appropriate party (14.30.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission establishing ownership is informal or the signing party is not shown to be authorized (37 CFR 3.73(b)), the terminal disclaimer is not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 14.16.02 or 14.16.03 as appropriate; if neither applies, provide a detailed statement of why there is no authorization and suggest corrective action (e.g., form paragraph 14.16.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/patent forming basis for double patenting rejection must be identified (14.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application or patent which forms the basis for the double patenting rejection must be identified in the terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no information is presented, use 14.32. If incorrect information is contained, use 14.26 and 14.26.05 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion to record assignment and use sample Certificate (14.34, 14.37–14.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an assignment document is submitted as the documentary evidence required by 37 CFR 3.73, it is suggested that the assignment document be submitted for recording among the Office assignment records (37 CFR 3.11; MPEP § 302).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enclose sample terminal disclaimers and a sample Certificate Under 37 CFR 3.73(b) (Part A for single assignment, Part B for chain of title). The certificate should be used the first time an assignee seeks to take action under 3.73(b). Parts and checkboxes (Copies of assignments, Reel/Frame, From/To fields) must be used as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer fee refund and non-duplication guidance (14.35–14.36.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant/patent owner is not required to pay another disclaimer fee when submitting a replacement or supplemental terminal disclaimer if a required fee was previously paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an additional fee was paid in error, applicant/patent owner may request a refund by submitting a written request and a copy of the Office action to the Commissioner of Patents and Trademarks, Office of Finance. If a refund has been authorized to a Deposit Account, make appropriate credit and do not use refund paragraph.
